name: Economic Residence Permit

requirements.blocker_text: Reported minimum investment of EC$400,000 in real estate, a bank deposit, or government bonds, maintained for at least 5 years; not independently confirmed against the governing regulation's text in this pass.
requirements.fix_path: Make and maintain a qualifying EC$400,000+ investment for at least 5 years.

requirements.blocker_text: Reported requirement to demonstrate net worth exceeding EC$400,000, plus an intention to invest in a commercial enterprise (no specific minimum reported for the commercial-enterprise component).

evidence_required.document: Proof of qualifying investment (real estate, bank deposit, or government bonds)

outcome.duration_length: not specified in the sources reviewed

sources.title: Montserrat Chapter 13.01, Immigration Act -- Section 19 (permit of economic residence, granted at Governor in Council's discretion; references subsidiary Immigration (Economic Residence Permit) Regulations, Section 39, S.R.O. 8/1998, in force 24 February 1998)

IMI Daily (residency/citizenship-by-investment industry outlet) -- reported Montserrat Economic Residence investment options (EC$400,000 in real estate, bank deposit, or government bonds) and net-worth requirement; this source itself cites no government document

notes: STATUS: DRAFT, part of Montserrat's initial build. This is the Section 19 sibling of ms_permanent_residence.json -- the Immigration Act itself confirms an 'economic residence' permit exists and names the governing subsidiary regulation (Immigration (Economic Residence Permit) Regulations, S.R.O. 8/1998), but the regulation's full text, containing the actual investment thresholds, was not located at tier-1 despite a dedicated search. The EC$400,000 figure and investment-type options here come from an industry/marketing outlet (IMI Daily) that itself cites no government source -- explicitly the weakest sourcing tier used in this pass, hence draft status; treat these figures as indicative, not confirmed. work_rights is 'restricted' as a conservative default consistent with other investment-residence routes in this dataset, not because the source stated a work-rights rule -- it did not. This route is distinct from ms_permanent_residence.json (residence-based, non-investment PR) and from ms_resident_permit_property_owner.json (a much lighter property-ownership status).
